The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 02.01.2022.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 02.01.2022 at about 4.30 p.m. while petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JK-1477, infront of Sri Sai Baba temple, near Kempegowda Arch,
Outer Ring Road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru City, Karnataka, at that time, the driver of the Cab bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AC-3740 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's motor cycle and as a result, petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.
Immediately, petitioner was shifted to People Tree hospital, then shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he took treatment for his accidental injuries as an inpatient.

It is stated that he has spent huge amount for his treatment, medicine etc.,
3.
It is further stated that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as Employee cum real estate broker and earning Rs.1,50,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work as doing earlier.
It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the Cab bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AC-3740.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the insurer and 2nd respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its learned counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 remained absent and hence, he was placed exparte.

sentences.text: The 1st respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
It has denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner and the amount spent towards medical expenses by the petitioner.

1st respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Cab bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-AC-3740 and contended that its liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.
It is contended that the insured of the offending vehicle has violated Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues :-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 02.01.2022 at about 4.30 p.m. while petitioner was riding the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JK-1477, infront of Sri Sai Baba temple, near Kempegowda Arch, Outer Ring Road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru City, Karnataka, at that time, the driver of the Cab bearing Reg. No.KA- 03-AC-3740 came from opposite direction on wrong lane and one way traffic by driving the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's motor cycle and as a result, petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, from who and how much?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked 21 documents as per Ex.P1 to 21.
On the other hand, respondent No.1 has examined one witness as RW.1 and he got marked 2 documents at Ex.R1 and R2.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the documents.
9.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
 Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 ... Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 ...
As per final order

sentences.text: Issues No.1:

As per the case of the petitioner, on 02.01.2022 at about 4.30 p.m. while petitioner was riding the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JK-1477, infront of Sri Sai Baba temple, near Kempegowda Arch, Outer Ring Road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru City, Karnataka, at that time, the driver of the Cab bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AC-3740 came from opposite direction on wrong lane and one way traffic by driving the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's motor cycle and as a result, petitioner sustained injuries.

The petitioner in order to prove his case, got examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of the petition and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, Spot Mahazar, Spot sketch, Notice and reply under Sec.133 of IMV Act, IMV Report and Charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to 8.
11.

According to the version of petitioner, the accident happened infront of Sri Sai Baba temple, near Kempegowda Arch, Outer Ring Road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru City, Karnataka at that time, the driver of the Cab bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AC-3740 came from opposite direction on wrong lane and one way traffic in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 and P4 being the Spot Mahazar and Sketch prepared at the time of mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 and 4 it reflects that the injured was proceeding in a motorcycle bearing No. KA-01-JK-1477, the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-03-AC-3740 came from opposite direction on wrong lane and one way traffic in a negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.

As per this document accident occurred on one way lane road, the offending vehicle driver has drove his car against the traffic rules, which makes it clear that the driver of Car by violating the traffic conditions came from opposite side in one way lane without observing up- coming vehicle dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.

If the driver of the car has not violated the traffic rules and also he driven it in a normal speed by observing on going vehicles on the road,
then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Further more, even the chargesheet as per Ex.P8 was also filed as against the driver of the Car.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P3 and 4 coupled with Ex.P8 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car.
12.
Even in the instant case the driver of the offending vehicle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part.

After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending Car bearing registration No.KA-03-AC-3740 concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
There is no reason to take a different view.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AC- 3740.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Cab bearing Reg. No.KA- 03-AC-3740.

Therefore,
the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.

sentences.text: LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:

It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as employee cum real estate broker and earning Rs.1,50,000/- per month and to prove the same, petitioner has produced Ex.P13 Service certificate.

On perusal of the said document, it reflects that the petitioner was working at Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru Rural and Ramanagara District Co-operative Milk Producers'
Society Union Ltd., Bengaluru.

sentences.text: But in proof of income petition has not produced any documents.
In the absence of document of income, the tribunal has to consider the notional income of the petitioner.
The incident occurred during the year 2022.
Considering the avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/- per month.
The petitioner claims that he is unable to work due to the injuries sustained to him.
The petitioner got examined the Doctor as PW.3.

In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained left proximal tibia fracture (Schatzker's Type 4 involving medial and lateral tibial plateau extending into TA Diaphyseal Region) and right leg lacerated wound and underwent open reduction internal fixation of left proximal tibia, lateral tibial condyle plate + AO Medial Condyle plate done on 04.01.2022.

On examination he found that the petitioner is facing difficulty to stand on both legs, waling on plain surface and slopes, climbing stairs, turning, squatting on floors, kneeling, sitting cross legged.
He assessed 36.64% disability to the left lower limb and 18.32% whole body disability of the petitioner.
While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on his work.
PW.3 is not a treated doctor and the disability assessed by him has to be taken into consideration carefully.
Hence, considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 12% disability to his whole body.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 59 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 02.01.2022.
However, by considering the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P11 Adhaar card as 01.02.1962, the petitioner was aged 60 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 60 is 9 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

15. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:

sentences.text: The wound certificate produced at Ex.P9 reflects the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
The doctor has opined that the said injuries are simple and grievous in nature.
The Ex.P10 Discharge Summary of People Tree Hospital reveals petitioner took treatment as out patient on 0.01.022.

Further the Inpatient record of Manipal Hospitals marked at Ex.17 discloses that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 02.01.2022 to 10.01.2022 wherein he underwent treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.50,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
16. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.30,960/- at Ex.P12.
I have examined the medical bills and receipts.

Further the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.30,960/- and he is entitled for the same.

17. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of 9 days, certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.10,000/- under this head.
18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least four months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.62,000/- (15,500X4) under this head.

19. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 60 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.
This court has considered disability to the extent of 12% to whole body.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.30,000/- on this head.
20. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
The doctor stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
Petitioner has to undergo surgery, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.

Thus he is entitled to Rs.30,000/- towards future medical and Puttaswamy vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160520931/

1. Loss of future earnings due to Rs. 2,00,880/- disability 2. Pain and Sufferings Rs. 50,000/-

3 . Medical expenses Rs. 30,960/-

nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental expenses.
5. Loss of income during laid up Rs. 62,000/- period 6. Loss of amenities in life/Life Rs. 30,000/- comforts and expectancy of life 7.

Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000/-
Total Rs. 4,13,840/-
In total, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,13,840/-.
22. Interest:
The petitioner is claiming interest @ 9% p.a. on the compensation amount.

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding future medical expenses) is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
23. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle Cab bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-AC-3740.

The insurance policy produced at Ex.R2 reflects that at the time of accident,
valid insurance policy was in force.
The breach of any of the policy conditions are not proved.
It is not disputed that 1st respondent is the insurer and 2nd respondent is the owner.
Hence, 1st respondent being the insurer and 2nd respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 1st respondent being the insurer shall indemnify the 2nd respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:

sentences.text: The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,13,840/-(Rupees Four lakhs thirteen thousand eight hundred and forty only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on Rs.3,83,840/-(excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the compensation amount, 70% of the award amount shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 30% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 2 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
